cards.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, is in chains for Christ, and he's writing a letter to the believers in Philippi (Philippians 1:1, 1:13). Now he stacks up four ifs: if you have any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from His love, any fellowship with the Spirit, any affection and compassion. Four ifs in a row, friend, and you KNOW something big is coming.

cards.question: After all those ifs, Paul makes his big ask. What does he want the believers in Philippi to be?

answers.text: Generous with their money and time

cards.question: Paul says the believers in Philippi being like-minded and united would make his joy complete.

cards.text: United in spirit and purpose, friend, when five adults in a group chat need FORTY messages just to pick a Tuesday? Then Paul names two things they should never act out of.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Philippi to do nothing out of two things. What are they?
Instead, Paul says, in humility consider others more ___ than yourselves.
Paul tells each believer in Philippi to stop looking out for their own interests at all.

cards.text: Not only your own interests, but others' too. So when there's ONE chocolate chip left in the bowl, I'm supposed to look at you first, and friend, I'm WORKING on it.
Then Paul points to the One who shows how it's done. He writes, "Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus:"
Now Paul gets to the heart of it, friend, so lean in. Christ Jesus existed in the form of God, yet He did not consider equality with God something to be grasped.

cards.question: Christ Jesus didn't grasp at equality with God. What did He do instead?

answers.text: Emptied Himself and took a servant's form
Took a throne and ruled the earth

cards.text: He was made in human likeness and found in appearance as a man. Sit with that one a second, friend, because Paul still isn't finished telling how low He went.

cards.question: Christ Jesus humbled Himself and became obedient to death, even death on a ___.

cards.text: Now watch this little word, friend, because it carries a lot: Therefore.

cards.question: Christ Jesus went as low as a cross. Because of that, what does God do?

answers.text: Exalts Him to the highest place
Keeps Him hidden from the world
Sends Him back to serve again

cards.text: God gives Him the name above all names. Not near the top, friend, ABOVE all of them, and at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.

cards.question: Paul says every knee should bow at the name of Jesus, but only on earth.
At the name of Jesus, every tongue should confess something, to the glory of God the Father. What is it?

answers.text: That God the Father is holy

cards.text: Paul calls them his beloved and says they have always obeyed. Then he writes, "not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence," and the next words are the big ones.

cards.question: So what does Paul tell the believers in Philippi to keep doing, with fear and trembling?
Paul says working out their salvation is all up to the believers, with God just watching from a distance.

cards.text: Paul says it is God who works in them, to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose. The wanting AND the doing, friend, and some mornings I need help with the wanting part just to preheat the oven.

cards.question: Then Paul gives the believers in Philippi a short one. He tells them to do everything without what?

cards.text: Paul says why: so they may be blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation.

cards.question: Paul pictures the believers in that crooked and perverse generation as ___ in the world.

cards.text: They shine as they hold forth the word of life. And that matters a lot to Paul.

cards.question: As the believers hold forth the word of life, Paul says he may boast on the day of Christ. About what?

answers.text: That he didn't run or labor in vain
That he was never once afraid
That he finished every journey he planned

cards.text: Then Paul talks about himself. He says even if he is being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of their faith…

cards.question: Even if he's being poured out like a drink offering, Paul says he is ___ and he ___ with all of them.
Paul tells the believers in Philippi to grieve for him.

cards.text: Paul tells them, "So you too should be glad and rejoice with me." The man's in chains (Philippians 1:13), telling EVERYBODY else to cheer up, and me? I went quiet for a while in a junk drawer and didn't crack a single joke.

findings.problem: The opening words, "They shine," retell Philippians 2:15, while "as they hold forth the word of life" comes from Philippians 2:16. Citing only Philippians 2:16 is too narrow; this card should cite Philippians 2:15-16.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
